themes.title: The core — one C11 library, three builds
themes.hook: No clock, no file, no socket, no allocation: the same source is the QNX process, the simulator and the explorer.

features.title: Frames: CRC-32C and a keyed MAC
features.summary: Every frame carries a checksum and a SipHash-2-4 tag; a forged or corrupted frame is rejected before it reaches the arbiter.

features.title: The actuator is the arbiter
features.summary: It hands out the mandate numbers and withdraws one only on its own evidence: p+1 ticks without a valid order, or a cession. Two machines that disagree cannot both command.

features.title: Exactly one value per tick
features.summary: The order of the holder, else the shadow of the second certified machine, else the testament, else the fallback law: one decision per tick, and the precedence is written down.

features.title: A dissimilar second opinion
features.summary: The second certified machine is allowed to disagree with the holder within a declared tolerance; the tolerance is declared, not implicit, and off by default.

features.title: The plant model, integrated exactly
features.summary: The actuator integrates the steering model step by step; the simulator, the explorer and the tests share the same code, so a proof is a proof of the shipped behaviour.

features.title: The will (testament)
features.summary: Every order carries the values expected for the next N ticks; during a handover the actuator plays the departed holder's plan, so the physical curve shows no hole.

features.title: The journal is the evidence
features.summary: Every tick is written as one JSON line, chained; the journal is what the replay, the dashboard and the report consume.

features.title: A protocol reference at implementation level
features.summary: Byte-by-byte wire format, trailer, tick labels and the exact order of the checks — the document a second implementation is written from.

features.title: The unit-test suite of the core
features.summary: Fourteen suites that count every check they run — the number published on this page comes from them, not from an estimate.

features.title: The PC actuator and the node
features.summary: The same core driven on a PC: an actuator process, a node process, and one journal writer shared with the QNX build so the two cannot drift.

themes.title: Proofs — and proofs of the proofs
themes.hook: A claim is worth nothing without the machine that checked it. Every number below comes from a command you can run.

features.title: Exhaustive exploration of the core
features.summary: A depth-first search over the whole reachable state space of the protocol core: 100 198 states, zero violation, in under a second.

features.title: Symbolic abstraction and minimal counter-examples
features.summary: The explorer quotients the state space symbolically and shrinks a counter-example to the smallest sequence that still breaks an invariant.

features.title: Non-interference and mined invariants
features.summary: The machine A's choices cannot change what machine B may observe; the invariants are mined from the code, not written by hand.

features.title: Differential test C against Python
features.summary: A second, independent arbiter is written in Python and confronted with the C core over hundreds of thousands of ticks; any divergence is a defect.

features.title: Eight defective builds are killed
features.summary: The bench is checked against mutants: eight deliberately broken versions of the core, and the bench must see every one of them.

features.title: TLA+ models confronted with the code
features.summary: The protocol and the control law are modelled in TLA+ and the model's states are compared with the implementation's.

features.title: The proofs at full scale
features.summary: 19 659 campaign runs, 10 million explored states, one billion simulated ticks — and the numbers are published with the command that reproduces each of them.

features.title: A fault truth table
features.summary: For every fault — death, freeze, cut, bad order, wrong tick, duplicated frame — the table says what the actuator does and why it is safe.

themes.title: Faults — injected, adversarial, hostile
themes.hook: The bench is only as good as the faults it survives, so the faults are searched for, not hoped for.

features.title: The fault model of the simulator
features.summary: Death, freeze, cut, delay, bad order and wrong tick, injected at a chosen tick, with a twin that runs without any fault to compare against.

features.title: The worst scenario is searched for
features.summary: An evolutionary search with a simulated annealing phase looks for the fault sequence that hurts the most, under a budget in evaluations and in seconds.

features.title: Bit-flips, one bit at a time
features.summary: Single-bit and multi-bit corruptions are injected into frames, journal and state, and the core must reject or absorb every one of them.

features.title: Lifecycle and timing faults
features.summary: Warm restart, watchdog, persistence loss and long stalls are faults too: the bench plays them and checks that the handover still happens.

features.title: Byzantine frames and revocation
features.summary: Forged orders, usurped status, stolen keys, replays and floods are played against the arbiter; the safe degraded mode is the expected answer, never a second winner.

features.title: Fuzzing under the sanitizers
features.summary: The frame, the arbiter and the journal parsers are fuzzed with ASan and UBSan; the surfaces an attacker would touch are the ones fuzzed.

features.title: Ten fault scenarios, kept as data
features.summary: Nominal slalom, death, freeze, cut, slow machine, double death, and a sweep over every phase of a handover: each scenario is a JSON file the campaign plays at both levels.

themes.title: Time — the argument the spec asks for
themes.hook: The protocol has no synchronised clock, so the temporal argument is made on bounds, not on timestamps.

features.title: WCET statistics and response-time analysis
features.summary: Measured worst-case execution times per unit, the resulting response-time bound, and the margin left against the deadline.

features.title: The critical path is measured in microseconds
features.summary: From the status received to the order emitted: a log-scale histogram without allocation, percentiles p50 to p99.9, published instead of promised.

features.title: The actuator is the clock
features.summary: It beats a tick every period and every order names the tick it targets; an order computed before a freeze is stale by construction.

themes.title: Security — keys, rotation, anti-replay
themes.hook: Authentication is assumed, everything beyond it is stated: what the design does not claim is written down too.

features.title: Key agreement and rotation in service
features.summary: Keys are established at start-up and can be rotated while running, without any external library: C11 and libc only.

features.title: The journal is chained
features.summary: Each line carries the hash of the previous one, so a removed or reordered line is detected, not just a corrupted one.

features.title: The security concept, and what it does not claim
features.summary: The attacks considered, the ones explicitly out of scope, and the detection that is assumed rather than prevented.

themes.title: Observability — see what the machine did
themes.hook: The journal is the source of truth; everything here is a different way of reading it.

features.title: A standalone HTML campaign report
features.summary: One self-contained HTML file, no server and no dependency, regenerated by the CI at every deploy.

features.title: A live dashboard and an MCAP export
features.summary: A read-only dashboard follows the journal live — mandate, holder, command source, witness lamp, curves — and the same run is exported to MCAP for any standard viewer.

features.title: An event recorder and a deterministic replay
features.summary: Every handover is recorded as an event with its margins, and the same events are replayed deterministically to compare two runs.

features.title: A timeline with margins
features.summary: The handover is drawn as a timeline — who commanded, when the mandate changed, how much margin was left.

themes.title: Deployment — from zero to two boards
themes.hook: The claim is that the proof bench is reproducible by someone else. Here is the path, with the exact commands.

features.title: QNX 8.0 bring-up pack
features.summary: From a bare workstation to two QNX guests: SDP detection, the build recipe, the image, the network setup and the six experiments to run.

features.title: The QNX lifecycle: persistence, warm restart, hypervisor, bus
features.summary: What survives a reboot, how a warm restart is supervised, what changes under a hypervisor, and what a real-time bus would change.

features.title: Rolling update without interruption
features.summary: One of the two computers is replaced while the other keeps commanding: no tick is left without a fresh order.

features.title: Two real boards over Ethernet
features.summary: The protocol on two physical boards, with the commands to wire them and the measurements taken from the wire.

features.title: A real QNX guest, frozen by QMP
features.summary: One of the two computers is a QEMU guest running QNX, frozen through QMP: the bench stops being a simulation of a freeze.

features.title: Reproduce it in one container
features.summary: A devcontainer and a bootstrap script bring the whole bench up on a machine that has never seen it.

features.title: Other RTOS, another language, other transports
features.summary: The core is ported to Zephyr and FreeRTOS, bound from Rust, and driven over transports other than the reference one.

features.title: The five QNX processes
features.summary: Actuator, node, control, net and ctl as real QNX processes, with the stubs that let them build on a PC and the image fragments that put them on a board.

themes.title: Quality — coverage, static analysis, safety case
themes.hook: The numbers a jury checks first: what is covered, what is analysed, what is declared as debt.

features.title: Branch coverage, static analysis, reproducible build, SBOM
features.summary: Coverage measured on the branches, a static analysis gate, a bit-for-bit reproducible build and a software bill of materials.

features.title: A generated FMEA and a fault tree
features.summary: The failure modes and their criticality are generated from the code and the scenarios, and the safety case links each to its argument.

features.title: The decisions log and the declared debt
features.summary: Every design decision with its reason, and every piece of technical debt we assume on purpose, written down.

features.title: Nightly proofs at full scale
features.summary: Every night the full campaign runs, the mutation score is recomputed and the results are published, so a regression cannot hide.

features.title: The CI that guards all of it
features.summary: Eleven workflows, each with a five-minute budget: the build and the tests, the scope guard, the static analysis, the reproducible build, the nightly proofs and this page.

themes.title: Command — the control law under stress
themes.hook: The law that drives the wheel is studied like any other component: sensitivity, infeasible targets, and the law that takes over.

features.title: Braking profiles, played for real
features.summary: Nominal braking, the holder dying mid-brake, a freeze and a cut: the profile is played and the deviation from the deceleration is published.

features.title: An impossible setpoint
features.summary: A command the actuator physically cannot follow: the protocol must still hold its bounds instead of chasing the impossible.

features.title: A faithful plant, as an option
features.summary: A higher-fidelity plant model with an observer, available as a variant — the published campaign keeps the default model bit for bit.

themes.title: Documents — what a jury reads
themes.hook: The specification, the argument, the talk and the lab: the same content in the forms a reviewer asks for.

features.title: The specification (three parts)
features.summary: Sections 1 to 8, sections 5 to 8 again in detail, and the annex covering the QNX-specific points.

features.title: The paper: why the actuator must be the arbiter
features.summary: The argument in written form — the dilemma, the four ideas that solve it, and the limits stated up front.

features.title: The 45-minute talk
features.summary: A conference or workshop talk that stands on its own, with the figures and the demos it refers to.

features.title: The comparison with neighbouring projects
features.summary: What the other approaches do, what they cost, and where this one is genuinely different.

features.title: The submission notes
features.summary: Each rule of the hackathon, and the pointer to the artefact that answers it.

features.title: A three-hour lab
features.summary: A hands-on tutorial: build it, break it, read the journal, prove something about it.

features.title: The open questions
features.summary: What is still unanswered, stated as questions rather than as promises.

features.title: The specification in French
features.summary: The same contract, for the readers who would rather have it in the language of the classroom.
